notes: §1985:XIII.3.3.4 GR2: between INITIATE and TERMINATE the report file is under RWCS control and 'no input-output statement may be executed which references that report file'; §1985:XIII.3.2.3 SR5 already limits a report file's references to USE, CLOSE and OPEN OUTPUT/EXTEND, so the run-time ban covers OPEN and CLOSE, whose violation 1985 leaves undefined. StatementValidation.ScreenReportFileReference refuses READ (COBOL2577) and CheckOpenModeForFile OPEN INPUT (COBOL2371); WRITE/REWRITE naming the file are refused (COBOL1639); a violating OPEN OUTPUT/EXTEND while active returns status 41 and the report continues (P7D, P7F), and EmitClose completes a violating CLOSE (2023's defined result, ReportWriter.IsActive read first; P7E: CLOSE 00, the later GENERATE writes nothing, final CLOSE 42), a permissible outcome of the undefined case. The witness runs the legal OPEN/INITIATE/GENERATE/TERMINATE/CLOSE order. Probes: b (each forbidden statement), e (OPEN OUTPUT and EXTEND of an open report file, the statements after the failed OPEN, CLOSE then GENERATE).

next.reason: The ban is the same, but the result of breaking it is now defined. 1985: between INITIATE and TERMINATE 'no input-output statement may be executed which references that report file'; 1985 XIII.3.3.3 SR3 already allows only USE, CLOSE and OPEN OUTPUT/EXTEND to name a report file, so the ban meant OPEN and CLOSE. 2023 §2023:13.18.46.4 GR2 'no OPEN or CLOSE statements shall be executed that reference the report file', with the same reference limit in §2023:13.18.46.3 SR3 and §2023:13.4.5.3 SR9 (the store's 'other I-O statements no longer refused' is wrong: they are refused at compile time in both). Difference: 1985 leaves a violating CLOSE undefined; 2023 §2023:14.9.6.4 GR5 completes the CLOSE and sets EC-REPORT-NOT-TERMINATED.
